name: Chimney sweep

pf.license.need: Sweeping and inspecting a chimney has no state license in most places. Where a state or city licenses chimney or home repair work, its form asks for it. Repairs (caps, crowns, liners, rebuilds) can need a contractor license or registration where the state or city requires one. Gas stove and insert work needs a gas fitter's license where the state licenses gas work. The hearth shop's counter: business registration only.
pf.license.who holds it: The company: its contractor license or registration, where the state's form asks. Each stove installer: a gas fitter's license, where the state licenses people. Sweeps and counter techs need none unless the state's form says so.
what to ask: The company's contractor license or registration number, where the state asks for one
Each stove installer's gas fitter's license number, in their invite reply
Proof of liability insurance, where the state's form asks for it
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.private certificates: A sweep's certificate from a trade group is not a state license. It shows in the business's own words, never as checked by Rosie.
pf.license.lead-safe work: Repairs that disturb paint in a home built before 1978 need a lead-safe certified firm, where the rules require it.
pf.license.renewals: Reminders before each expiry, on the dates the owner picks. A lapsed license pauses new bookings for that work or person.
pf.license.background checks: Only where the state's form asks.
pf.license.local rules: Some cities need a permit for a liner, a rebuild or a new stove: the form for that place applies, by the customer's address.

pf.services.skills each needs: Level 2 inspections need the flue camera. Gas stove work needs a gas fitter. Masonry repairs need the masonry skill. Custom caps and casting repairs need Rory.

pf.services.season: Fall books up weeks ahead. The owner can set a fall deposit and a list for sooner times (see the gaps).
pf.services.extras: Travel inside the service area only (the example: 25 miles). Parts at the owner's list. No tax line unless the owner sets a rate.

pf.safety.general screen: Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first.

pf.visit.check-in at the customer's place: The check-in code at the door. The on-my-way text names the sweep, with a photo.
pf.visit.check-in at the counter: The code at the counter. A drop-off gets its code when the door is left, and READY when it's done.
pf.visit.roof: Roof work only when it's dry and not windy. Otherwise the sweep works from the firebox, and checks the crown and cap from the ladder with a camera pole. If that isn't enough, a roof check is booked again for free.
pf.visit.what a Level 1 covers: The firebox, damper, smoke chamber, the flue that can be seen, the crown and the cap. Drop cloths and a hearth vacuum, and photos before and after.
pf.visit.quotes at the visit: A leak is quoted with its lines before any work. The customer may OK part of it. The quote stays good 7 days.
pf.visit.findings: Nothing is repaired at a sweep unless it's quoted and OK'd. A rain cap can go on the same day if the customer says yes. Bigger repairs get a written quote with photos, and their own day. Over the owner's limit (the example: $500), the owner OKs it first.
pf.visit.a hazard found: Like cracked flue tiles: a written no-use notice at once (no fires until it's repaired), kept with the photo report.
pf.visit.work sold at the home: A written right to cancel, where the rules require it.
pf.visit.proof it's done: DONE with the bill's lines and the after photos. The photo report goes with the receipt. A Level 2's camera report comes later, by the date given.

pf.rules.lead-safe work: Lead-safe work rules for older homes: where the rules require it.

pf.rules.live animals: The business doesn't remove live animals. A wildlife company does it first, licensed where the state requires one.
pf.rules.license on papers: The license number on quotes and bills: from the state form.
pf.rules.declared emergency: Price limits in a declared emergency: where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.warranty: The owner's own, shown on the receipt.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, as for every kind of work.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for chimney work:
chimney: A chimney fire or a CO alarm at any point: get out and call 911 first; the owner is told
Signs of an old chimney fire: no fires until a Level 2, with the owner's OK
Animals or nesting birds in the chimney: a wildlife company first; the sweep can move with no fee
Wet or windy on the day: worked from the firebox and the ladder; a roof check booked again for free
Cracked flue tiles found: a written no-use notice, then a quote for a liner
A bigger repair found (a cracked crown, no cap): its own written quote, OK'd by the owner over the limit, on another day
Fall rush: openings weeks out; a freed time goes to people who asked for a sooner one
Nobody home at the door: the no-show steps, with the owner's OK before any fee
At the counter: a door that can't be refit, a gas part, or a drop-off nobody picks up

notes:
Pilot: plumber (from). A sweep's home visit runs like the plumber's: 2-hour arrival windows, the trip fee held, list prices set by the answers (per flue, the inspection level), findings quoted at the visit or as their own job, and a counter at the shop. The cleaner (the service pilot) was weighed: its set price and plan fit, but its rug drop-off and crew-of-two cleans don't, and inspection-then-repair is the plumber's quote path.
Flow B is the usual side: Lee Chimney Sweeps, Sam's main company: chimney sweeping (sweeps, Level 1 and Level 2 inspections, caps, crowns, leaks, liners), and stove work as the second kind of work (the master's electrical): gas stove and insert work, licensed where the state licenses gas work. Wes Carter (sweep and gas fitter) and Dale Ortiz (sweep) are the master's Jordan and Casey. 75 Mill Rd; Alex's home is 9 Cedar Ln.
Flow A is the less usual side: Lee Hearth Shop, Sam's second company (the master's Lee's Barbershop), a stove and chimney parts counter. Customers bring a stove door for a new gasket or glass, pick up a stainless cap sized to their flue (the cap fitting, paid in full), or leave a door for a rebuild. Rory Chen (custom caps, home visits) and Shay Diaz are the master's Riley and Avery. 310 Grove St.
Example prices are the example businesses' own and keep the master's amounts, so sums add up. B: $89 trip fee (held; the late-cancel and nobody-home fee), $179 sweep and Level 1 (first flue; $79 each extra flue), $150 wood stove sweep, $640 crown repair from photos ($160 deposit), a leak priced at the visit ($245: flashing $165, crown seal $80), a $199/$249 Level 2 by person, a $160 rain cap and a $95 damper repair as extra work, a $900 crown rebuild, a $2,400 liner in stages.
A: $35 gasket refit ($75 at home), $40 stove glass, $20 door handle, $25 ash pan repair, $55 cap fitting (paid in full), $140 stove door rebuild (2½ hours; the $40 fee held, or a $40 deposit), a $90 custom cap from photos, a casting repair after a $25 look.
Money B: the main path is list|hold|bill, the plug-in's starting answer. The old example took a $50 fall deposit only because card holds expired; with day-before holds, the fall deposit is the owner's season choice: list|deposit|bill ($40 on the $150 stove sweep; B5-11 words say it's the fall one). list|none|bill is the off-season. visit|hold|bill is a chimney leak priced at the visit; photos|deposit|bill a crown repair from photos. No card-only or charge-at-DONE path: the old flowchart was paid on completion by card on the sweep's phone, a link or a check, which is Rosfield's bill.
Money A: the plumber pilot's counter set: list|card|counter (main), none, hold, deposit, full (the cap fitting picked up), photos (a custom cap), visit (a casting repair).
Chimney work is never sent now: a fire now is a 911 call, never a booking (S2-30, B4-81, B4-16, B6-03, B7-55, B8-58 off).
Level 2: one booked for a home sale, a new stove or fuel, or signs of an old fire asks Sam first (B6-03 more; the old 'Greta confirms these herself'). A Level 2 added to a booked sweep (B7-31) is a list price with no OK.
License: no state is named. S1-60 and S2-28 keep both branches: chimney repair is licensed where the state or city licenses it (the example: the company's contractor license CR045210), gas stove work licenses the company and each installer (GS22871; Wes's GF30417), and sweeps and counter techs need none. The hearth shop gives its registration (S1-63's license branch off). Rename pairs carry this into S1-23, S1-39, S1-49, S1-50 and S2-05 to S2-28.
A trade group's sweep certificate isn't a state license: it shows only as checked (S13-11; pf.license).
Own steps: B7-x01 (animals in the chimney: damper shut, no fire, a wildlife company first; protected nesting birds stay until they leave) and A8-x01 (a warped door that can't be refit: a new door, or a sweep at home). Words: B3-18 and B3-19 (signs of an old fire; a fire now), B8-30 (cracked flue tiles: a written no-use note), B8-31 (a wet roof: swept from the firebox, the top checked from the ladder), B5-11 (the fall deposit), and the pilot's A4-29, A4-67, A7-13, A7-60, reworded. More: B4-05, B4-07, B4-44, B5-21, B6-03, B7-17, B8-18, B10-01, B10-24, A4-36.
Off in B as well: a plan or warranty that pays, and insurance (B4-43, B4-63, B7-05, B9-19: the customer pays, and a claim after a chimney fire is the customer's own, with the receipt and photo report), a rented fan (B10-07), an outside check partway (B8-65). Flow A's plan and insurance what-ifs are off too (review, Oct 22): the hearth shop bills none.
Plug-in splits kept whole (splitsKept): S1-60 and S2-28 in both flows (state by state). A: A7-59, S11-87, S11-90 (a drop-off names no counter tech), A7-61 (custom caps are Rory's alone), A8-02 (a refit needs the stove door), A8-53 (at the counter, or a drop-off). B: B4-57 (a written estimate above the plug-in's amount), B8-69 and B8-70 (a cap or crown from the roof with nobody home; a sweep needs someone home), B8-71 (a new wood stove delivered and set up, stove work), B8-72 (a stove door to the shop), B10-29 (a permit inspection for a liner, a rebuild or a new stove).
Times read as 2-hour arrival windows (B4-83 '1'); the old flowchart's set visit times (8, 10, 1, 3) fit them. A crew of two stays for liners and rebuilds (B7-56).
Plans: the master's yearly flush plan is a yearly wood stove sweep plan ($150, as the master's form says). The old flowchart's August text to pick a September time is a more line on B4-44 and B5-21; picking each visit when it comes up is a gap. Flow A's plan is a yearly door check (the master's every-4-weeks haircut plan).
keep: 'leak' is chimney work's own word (a chimney leak repair, a leak by the chimney).
Sentence pairs rename the master's plumbing and barbershop examples where words alone would read wrong (the questions that set the price, the reminder's prep line, the quote lines, the notes, the receipts, the warranty claims). The receipt's warranty is the example's own: a 30-day sweep guarantee, and 1 year on repairs.
Unsure: walk-in drop-offs at the hearth shop are kept, like the plumber's counter; the second kind of work could as well be dryer vent cleaning (no license), which would need words ops on S1-39 instead of renames.
Review (Oct 22): flow A's plan, insurance, rental and later-result branches are off (the counter bills no plan, rents nothing, and has no later result). B's S11-56 now moves the wood stove sweep from the $89 hold to the $40 fall deposit (the plug-in's own choice), not from a full price it never takes. A sweep takes 2 hours, so DONE, the bill and the receipt come after 10am (B8-41, B9-06, B10-01, B8-32's part run). Rename pairs: '2½-hour stove door rebuild' (A3-02) and 'Only Wes repairs crowns' (B8-34, photos path).
Review (Oct 22): side branches the work never has are off too, where their own step said so: the live line (B3-01), seats at a host's place (B4-43), an expert's read (B6-03, A6-01), weather at the counter (A7-02), a class roster (A8-03), a counter visit over several days (A8-32). The plug-in now names nothing taken at the counter (A list|none|counter), which the money paths already listed.
Review, round 2 (Oct 22): the permit-inspection what-if uses a new stainless liner, work the plug-in says needs a permit (B10-29, B10-24), and Dale's skills read 'chimney and stove sweeps and leak repairs' (B4-17, B7-17, B7-19, B7-54).
touch-up 4 (Oct 23): keep 'drips': water that drips by a chimney when it rains, and checking for drips after a crown repair, are real chimney words.
